cryptohome: Bind Downloads to MyFiles/Downloads Change cryptohome to create two new folders inside user's cryptohome. MyFiles and MyFiles/Downloads. This is part of the work to allow users to manager files and folders inside MyFiles in the File Manager. This will change the local volume from being Downloads to be MyFiles, which is controlled by the flag "MyFilesVolume" in the Chromium browser side. Change cryptohome to bind mount Downloads to MyFiles/Downloads in all user's homes. Without mounting these 3 options, it would make these user folders to have inconsistent view of the user's Downloads. - /home/chronos/u-<user_hash> - /home/user/<user_hash> - /home/chronos/user Failing to bind mount any of the Downloads mentioned above makes |MountHomesAndDaemonStores| return false and in turn makes |MountEphemeralCryptohomeInner| and |MountEphemeralCryptohomeInner| return false, which means that it failed to mount guest and normal user respectively. This change continues to mark Downloads folder as tracked directory and also adds MyFiles and MyFiles/Downloads as tracked directories. To my knowledge these folders aren't yet used as tracked in other routines, however this enables us to improve the low-storage cleanup to choose these folders for specific cleanup policies, but this is work is outside this CL and not planned yet. ARC++ continue to mount the same Downloads, so no changes required for it. Marking COMMIT=False until Chromium side is ready to read from the new Downloads location. Tests: New unittest for cryptohome. Additionally I manually tested in 2 devices with arc and arc-next. retry.py: add exponential backoff In server side autotest power_ServoV4ChargeWrapper, we would like to be able to send command to Servo v4 to control whether it is a power source or sink for the DUT. After sending the command, we would like to check that the command we send is actually effective, by querying the power role of Servo v4, and by checking the DUT power status. It usually take around 1 second for the change to take effect, so we need a retry decorator to keep querying until success or timeout. Exponential backoff in the retry decorator helps us reduce the number of times to retry, but still responds fast if Servo v4 command succeeds quickly. Thus, we are adding the option to exponentially increase delay time, while preserving the randomization. CRAS: Do not mix stream before its first fetching When we add the new stream, the next_cb_ts of this stream would be set to the earliest next_cb_ts of others. It causes the new stream keep empty before next fetch time. It also means we can not write any frames during this time. However, if we use the big client buffer and the small device buffer, the next fetch time is far from now. It will trigger underrun. Hence, we need to ignore new stream until it starts fetching and running. In order to do it, we create new stream list "pending_streams" for each device. First, we add the new streams in this list. And then move streams from pending_streams to the original stream list when they request fetching. So the new streams will not affect other streams anymore. BUG=b:117915490 TEST=Playing two streams does not trigger underruns on grunt.
